research_concepts: play-type possession records derived from play-by-play
role portability across regular season and playoffs
methodological_questions: Is 'travel' (role portability across contexts) defined operationally before testing, and is it measurable for each unit?
Do play-type labels derived from outcome-linked play-by-play have adequate validity for CUT and DRIVE shares?
Do cut-heavy and drive-heavy role profiles differ in cross-context stability after controlling for team and season effects?
Is n=24 units enough to detect a group difference in portability at useful power?

historical_evidence.finding: Play-type label backfill verification. Recorded result: PNR 28.7% FAIL (band 20-28%); PULL_UP 7.9% FAIL; 3100 games with team PNR >33% FAIL; PNR PPP 0.948 PASS; temporal PASS; team identity FAIL; 2024-25 PULL_UP ~0-1% for many teams. Final recorded as FAIL. 82.8% of PNR labels were proxy_calibrated. Failure mechanism recorded as C_artifact.

Play-type label accuracy/distribution audit. Overall FAIL: OTHER 20.2% vs <10% target; 40.8% low confidence; DRIVE foul-draw 1.7% vs 14-22% benchmark; most play types have PPP above benchmark band; MIA identity checks fail. Foul possessions leak into OTHER. Verdict recorded as tool_eval_fail.

Persistent Impact Score lag curves. Global lifts for DRIVE/SPOT_UP/TRANSITION were flat and non-decaying; after team-season demeaning, within-team memory was essentially none except SPOT_UP lag-1 (+0.027 globally). PNR lag-1 within-team lift -0.0218. Recorded as artifact.

Persistent Impact Score Level 1 gate. Failed decay-sanity: DRIVE lifts flat across lags (+0.015 to +0.021); within-team lag-1 +0.015 to -0.002; Cohen d ~0.01-0.03 with p~0 from n>150k. Verdict recorded as failed_gate; limitation recorded as team-quality confounding.

Regular season vs playoff PPP by play type. DRIVE RS 1.198 vs PO 0.912 (-0.286, 25 teams, min 30 possessions per cell); PNR -0.173; PULL_UP +0.301; others within -0.07. No CIs reported. Recorded as D_positive and supported; it motivated the playoff DRIVE exclusion.

Defensive scheme extractor. On four games, 759 matchup rows had zero non-zero switchesOn values (SWITCH feed empty). ICE_CANDIDATE labels were not confirmed without screen-contact tracking; HEDGE/TRAP/ZONE unlabeled. Verdict recorded as tool_eval_fail.

PNR shot-level season rates vs possession labels. 2024-25 shot-level PNR share of half-court shots ranged from 7.6% (OKC) to 13.8% (IND) across 30 teams. No pass/fail gate; rates were a calibration input for PBPProxyPNR. Failure mechanism recorded as E_unclear.

State persistence vs window-overlap null (pre-registered). Process-only lag-1 r=+0.645 vs null +0.655; excess -0.010, cluster-bootstrap 95% CI [-0.012,-0.009]; N=1,060,893 possessions. Recorded as B_powered_null: state persistence does not clear the overlap null.

Defensive Style Index shift RS vs playoffs. SWITCH 0.294 to 0.336; DROP 0.399 to 0.343; HELP 0.307 to 0.321 recorded as 'No meaningful shift'. Per-team shifts range -0.287 to +0.271 with no test; 32 team-seasons; no CIs. Failure mechanism recorded as E_unclear.

A1 adaptation falsification (asymmetry, confidence, carryover). Adapter dPPP +0.067 (n=205), wrong_way +0.011 (n=274), no_signal +0.126 (n=57); next-game PPP Welch t=-1.003, p=0.842. Recorded as C_artifact; limitations recorded as label error and selection/regression to the mean.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Backfilled play-type labels as a valid basis for play-type analysis (PNR and PULL_UP shares, team identity).
failed_approaches.why: Recorded failures: PNR share outside band, PULL_UP shares near 0-1% for many teams in 2024-25, team identity FAIL; labels are largely proxy-calibrated. Recorded mechanism: C_artifact.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Inferred play-type labels as a benchmark-consistent classification of possessions.
failed_approaches.why: OTHER share 20.2% vs <10% target; 40.8% low confidence; foul possessions leak into OTHER; DRIVE foul-draw rate far below benchmark. Recorded as tool_eval_fail, noting that label systematic issues undermine adaptation findings.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Play-type lag effects (action memory) as evidence of persistent role influence.
failed_approaches.why: Global lifts were flat and non-decaying and vanished after team-season demeaning. Recorded mechanism: C_artifact.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Decay-sanity gate for DRIVE cross-possession memory.
failed_approaches.why: Lifts were flat across lags; effect sizes were negligible (d ~0.01-0.03); team-quality confounding was recorded. Verdict failed_gate.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using the box-score switchesOn feed and ICE_CANDIDATE labels to classify defensive schemes.
failed_approaches.why: switchesOn was zero in all 759 rows; ICE_CANDIDATE was not confirmed without screen-contact tracking. Verdict tool_eval_fail.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Adaptation-response test using play-type-derived scheme labels.
failed_approaches.why: Wrong-way and no-signal group contrasts were inconsistent with the adaptation hypothesis; next-game PPP showed no carryover (p=0.842). Recorded as C_artifact with label error and regression to the mean as limitations.

evidence_establishes: Play-type labels derived from this project's play-by-play pipeline have recorded validity failures (FAM:SF-APPA-030, FAM:SF-APPM-014), so any CUT/DRIVE share used as the role variable is at risk of label error.
Past play-type memory and adaptation effects in this pipeline were recorded as artifacts once team-level confounding or label error was addressed (FAM:SF-APPS-073, FAM:SF-CHT-029, FAM:SF-APPA-001).

A team-level regular-season vs playoff PPP contrast for DRIVE was recorded as supported on 25 teams (FAM:SF-APPS-011). This is the only retrieved positive finding that bears on context change for drive-type possessions.
The defensive-role and switch fields needed for role classification are not reliably populated in the retrieved feed (FAM:SF-APPM-053).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether cut-heavy shapers' roles are more or less portable than drive-heavy shapers' roles. No retrieved record tests this comparison.
Whether a 'shaper' or 'role' has been operationally defined in earlier work. No retrieved record defines these terms for this question.
Whether the 25-team DRIVE regular-season vs playoff gap in FAM:SF-APPS-011 holds after label repair or CI estimation; it reported no CIs and used labels later flagged as unreliable.
Any portability estimate at n=24 units, or any effect size for CUT-heavy vs DRIVE-heavy profiles.
own_inferences: 'Travel' is undefined. Without an operational definition (for example, a stability correlation of role profile across regular season and playoffs, or out-of-context predictive transfer), the question cannot be tested.

The retrieved DRIVE playoff-decline finding (FAM:SF-APPS-011) rests on the same play-type labels that FAM:SF-APPA-030 and FAM:SF-APPM-014 recorded as failing validation. Its support status is therefore weaker than its record suggests.

With 24 units and per-unit play-type shares that come from noisy derived labels, the design is likely to be underpowered and sensitive to team-level confounds, as the demeaning results in FAM:SF-APPS-073 and FAM:SF-CHT-029 suggest.
CUT labels may be less affected by foul leakage than DRIVE labels, which may make the comparison asymmetric. This is a hypothesis, not a recorded finding.
uncertainties: No retrieved record gives the per-unit definition of cut-heavy or drive-heavy shares, or the exact 24 units (teams or players).
Record statuses differ between auto_outcome_status and observed final verdicts (for example, FAM:SF-APPA-030 is auto inconclusive but final FAIL). This review follows the recorded status fields.
The number of retrieved records is 10 and they are consolidated family summaries; full text was not read for most, so some limitations may be missing.
Playoff data for 2025-26 was complete from 2026-06-21, but the playoff label quality for that season was not reported in any retrieved record.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved label-validity failures (FAM:SF-APPA-030, FAM:SF-APPM-014) and the recorded artifact outcomes for play-type memory and adaptation analyses (FAM:SF-APPS-073, FAM:SF-CHT-029, FAM:SF-APPA-001) show that play-type-based role measures on this pipeline have not passed validation. Together with the undefined 'travel' construct and n=24, this moves the decision from a plain test to do_not_proceed as posed. A minimum viable test with label validation and an operational portability definition is described in design.

blocking_constraints.text: CUT and DRIVE shares come from derived play-type labels with recorded validity failures (FAM:SF-APPA-030, FAM:SF-APPM-014).
n=24 units is likely too few to detect a group difference in portability at useful power, and the record shows no power analysis for this question.
Play types are derived from play-by-play outcomes (points, PPP), so role measures and outcome measures are not independent.
Team-quality and team-season effects were recorded as confounders that collapsed earlier effects (FAM:SF-CHT-029, FAM:SF-APPS-073).

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests whether cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones. The closest work is a team-level RS vs playoff DRIVE PPP contrast (FAM:SF-APPS-011, supported, no CIs) that rests on labels later flagged in FAM:SF-APPA-030 and FAM:SF-APPM-014. Other records address play-type memory, state persistence, defensive scheme and adaptation, which are related but not the same question.

risks.text: Play-type labels fail validation (PNR and PULL_UP share errors; OTHER leakage; team identity failures) per FAM:SF-APPA-030 and FAM:SF-APPM-014.
Labels are built from outcome-linked play-by-play, so role shares and PPP-based portability measures are coupled.
n=24 units; no power analysis; CI-free prior findings (FAM:SF-APPS-011).
Team quality and team-season effects produced artifacts in earlier analyses (FAM:SF-CHT-029, FAM:SF-APPS-073).
Per-unit play-type shares over a season may be noisy; the reliability of role profiles across contexts is unknown.
Playoff samples per unit are smaller than regular-season samples, so role profiles in playoffs may be unstable (inferred from playoff possession counts; not directly recorded).
Units selected for extreme cut or drive shares may regress toward the mean in the other context, which would mimic portability differences.
A null or near-zero portability gap can arise from the structure of the measure, as in the overlap-null result FAM:SF-APPS-069.
Play-type labelling and calibration change across seasons (for example, 2024-25 PULL_UP shares near zero), so cross-season comparison is confounded by label drift.

design.estimand: Not defined as posed. Minimum viable estimand: the difference between cut-heavy and drive-heavy units in the stability (cross-context correlation or out-of-context predictive transfer) of their role profile between regular season and playoffs, with the stability measure fixed before analysis.
design.unit: Team-season or player-season unit, fixed before analysis. Units must be chosen so that the cut-heavy vs drive-heavy classification is defined before the context comparison.
design.sample: Minimum viable sample: all 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular-season and playoff units with complete data, from 2025-26 playoffs only after 2026-06-21. The 24 recorded units are insufficient on their own and should be pooled across seasons with season and team as clusters.
design.power: Not established. A pre-registered power analysis must be run before any test. Given n=24 units and the noise in derived shares, the minimum detectable difference is expected to be large; if it cannot reach useful power, the study should be reported as underpowered rather than as a null.
design.controls: Team-season fixed effects; team quality (for example, net rating) as a covariate; play-type label validation gate using the benchmark checks in FAM:SF-APPM-014 and identity checks in FAM:SF-APPA-030 before analysis; foul-possession exclusion from OTHER; reliability split-half of role profiles; regression-to-the-mean correction using a holdout season.
design.falsification: Pre-registered null: no difference in cross-context stability between cut-heavy and drive-heavy units, with a cluster-bootstrap CI. Also a placebo: the same stability test on a non-role metric (for example, shot-distance mix) should show no group difference.
design.multiplicity: Single primary contrast pre-registered; secondary contrasts (per-season, per-play-type) labelled exploratory and corrected for multiple testing.
design.decision_rule: Proceed to a confirmatory test only if the label validation gate passes on the chosen units and the power analysis reaches a pre-specified threshold. If the validation gate fails, report the result as an artifact-risk outcome, not as a finding. If power is insufficient, report as untestable at this sample size.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular season and playoffs per the data description. 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13; 2025-26 playoffs complete from 2026-06-21 only. Label pipeline version must be frozen and recorded before analysis.

research_concepts: role portability across seasons and playoffs
methodological_questions: Do role profiles based on cut versus drive frequency transfer across regular season and playoff contexts?
How many units (players or teams) are needed to test a group difference in role portability?
How should role stability be measured given small units n=24?
What risks arise from deriving play-type labels from outcome-linked play-by-play?
args.query: Cut-heavy shapers versus drive-heavy shapers: role portability across seasons and playoffs, with n=24 units, play-by-play derived play-type possession records

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-08-08, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=24

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}
